minutes.headline: Assessors voted to recommend against the residential and small commercial exemptions and for a single tax rate.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors reviewed the principal assessor's status report (interim values approved, tax rate delayed by MUNIS data problems). They also reworked the exemption warrant article slides and the classification hearing presentation, and discussed hiring a third party to redo neighborhood codes. They approved prior minutes and settled their recommendations for the select board's classification hearing.

public_comment.topic: Chair called for public comment; none was offered and no one was on Zoom.
Second call for public comment at the end; none.

votes.outcome: passed (all in favor, none opposed; count not stated)

budget_items.what_was_said: Interim values were approved by the Department of Revenue; single-family values and total valuation rose, with commercial higher.
The levy is unknown because the finance director has not finished entering data in Gateway amid MUNIS problems, putting the November 19th classification hearing at risk.
New growth was certified on the LA-13.
An annual software maintenance bill from Vision was mentioned for signature.

budget_items.topic: Value of the temporary assessing staffer
budget_items.what_was_said: Board members said the staffer's catch of missed value brought in revenue exceeding the cost of keeping her.

budget_items.topic: Cost of adopting COLA clauses for exemptions
budget_items.what_was_said: The warrant listed zero cost, but the assessor said there is a cost to the town, to be confirmed; the increase falls on other taxpayers via the overlay.
Income and asset limits were discussed for the chart on the exemption slides.
Median single-family value passed half a million dollars for the first time, up about 5%.

budget_items.topic: Tax rate scenarios for split rate
budget_items.what_was_said: Scenarios using last year's levy show a CIP shift greatly raises commercial bills while barely lowering residential bills.
A cost figure was mentioned in passing, unclear in the captions.

decisions.decision: An exemptions outreach conference will go on the Nov. 20 agenda, with the chair given leave to follow up with the senior center, aiming for early January.
Review of the October 2 and October 16 minutes postponed to the next meeting.
The board agreed in principle to pursue a third-party review of neighborhood codes via an RFP and funding request, with details to come later; waterfront fixes may be done in-house.
The board will advise the select board to reject the residential exemption and small commercial exemption, take no position on open space discount, and recommend a single tax rate.
A public information release will be posted on the town website.
Next meeting set for Nov. 20 and a tentative meeting in early December; Dec. 18 was floated.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors settled its advice to the select board: reject the residential exemption and the small commercial exemption, and recommend a single tax rate.
The recorded votes on those items were not audible, so the minutes cannot give a tally; the single-rate recommendation came near the end of the classification discussion.
The principal assessor reported that the tax rate is delayed because the finance director has not finished entering data amid MUNIS problems, which puts the Nov. 19 classification hearing at risk.
The board agreed in principle to seek a third-party review of neighborhood codes through an RFP and a funding request, with details to come.
Scenarios for a split rate, run on last year's levy, showed a shift to commercial greatly raising commercial bills while barely lowering residential bills.

why_it_matters: The select board's classification hearing decides whether homes and small businesses get an exemption and whether commercial property is taxed at a higher rate, so this advice bears on the share of the levy that falls on a household's bill.
If the tax rate is not set in time for the hearing, the timing of the hearing and the tax bills that follow could slip, a result of data entry problems in the town's accounting system.
watch_next: Select board classification hearing, listed for Nov. 19 but at risk while the levy remains unentered.
Assessors' next meeting on Nov. 20, with a tentative early-December meeting (Dec. 18 floated).
